result:
No, this needs changes before publishing. Two problems:

1. **"fully compliant with the framework"** — NIST SP 800-61 is a guidance document (the Computer Security Incident Handling Guide), not a certifiable standard with a compliance checklist like PCI-DSS or ISO 27001. There's no formal "compliance" to claim. This is an unsubstantiated and somewhat meaningless assertion as written, and it's the kind of claim a security-savvy reader (or a customer's legal/procurement team) will immediately push back on. Better: "Our workflow is informed by / aligned with NIST SP 800-61" or specify *which* phases/practices you follow (e.g., "we structure our workflow around the SP 800-61 lifecycle: preparation, detection & analysis, containment/eradication/recovery, and post-incident activity").

2. **The uncited conference talk** — Don't publish an admission that you're citing a source you can't produce. In public docs this reads as either sloppy or an unverifiable appeal to authority, and undercuts trust in the rest of the doc. Options: drop the reference entirely (just describe the practice itself, e.g., "and incorporates common SRE incident-response patterns"), or track down the actual talk/speaker/conference and cite it properly. Don't ship "no citation handy" as if it's acceptable sourcing.

Suggested rewrite:

> "Our workflow is structured around the NIST SP 800-61 incident-handling lifecycle (preparation, detection & analysis, containment/eradication/recovery, and post-incident activity), and incorporates common SRE incident-response practices such as [specific practice, e.g., blameless postmortems, structured on-call rotations]."

This is accurate, verifiable, and doesn't overstate compliance you can't back up.
